name: Blood Mountain
where: Byron Reece trailhead on US 19/129 near Neel Gap, south of Blairsville, Georgia
blurb: The highest point of the Appalachian Trail in Georgia, with a 1934 stone shelter on top: a walk to Flatrock Gap, the summit hike on the rerouted Byron Reece Trail, and the Freeman Trail loop around the mountain.

trails.name: Byron Reece Trail to Flatrock Gap
Blood Mountain via the Byron Reece Trail
Blood Mountain Loop via the Freeman Trail

status: Open. The Byron Herbert Reece Trail was rerouted and reopened on June 6, 2026; the old route is closed and the new one meets the A.T. a quarter mile southwest of Flatrock Gap. The trailhead lot is small and fills early; no hiker parking at Walasi-Yi. Overnight campers between Jarrard Gap and Neel Gap need a hard-sided bear canister March 1 to June 1.

rare.why: It lives only in the Chattahoochee and Nantahala national forests of north Georgia and western North Carolina and is rated vulnerable by NatureServe; it is the most-recorded amphibian around these trails in iNaturalist.

notes: Distances are measured on OSM along the 2026 reroute (OSM way 1546306916, 1.32 mi); no official post-reroute totals were published yet (GATC says the new trail is 1.2 mi, ATC says 1.4 mi). Pre-reroute guides list 4.3 mi for the summit and about 6 mi for the Freeman loop. Ruffed grouse and the Chattahoochee slimy salamander have no fauna.py model; both are added as small custom models through animals_js/extra_js. Animals documented (iNaturalist within 2.5 km, wilderness.net) but not modeled: copperhead (mentioned in the rattlesnake card), other salamanders (Ocoee, seal, blackbelly), dark-eyed junco, black-throated blue warbler, ovenbird, eastern towhee, barred owl. Summit shelter position is placed beside the OSM peak node (no OSM node for the shelter); its orientation follows the A.T. at the summit, not verified. Walasi-Yi Center is not modeled because it falls in the flattened outer band of the tile.
